mn102:2.9: This does not mean Nibbāna in the Buddhist sense; see 25.1 below, and see Sutta 75 (Māgandiya) for one who holds this view.
mn102:3.1: Kasiṇa, translated in Sutta 77 as ‘totality’ or ‘wholeness’.
mn102:4.5: The cessation of formations means Nibbāna (Comy).
mn102:6.1: Some editions read ‘tesaṁ ete’ here and at the parallel passages rather than ‘tesaṁ eke’; the sense is not materially affected.
mn102:7.4: The reading ‘ahaṁ aññatra rūpā aññatra vedanāya aññatra saññāya aññatra saṅkhārehi viññāṇassa āgatiṁ…’ has been preferred here; cf. Saṁyutta XXII, 53-4.
mn102:10.3: The compound diṭṭha-suta-muta-viññātabba has been resolved as ‘what has been seen, heard, sensed, and cognized’, though it could also be rendered ‘what is to be cognized as seen, heard, and sensed’.
mn102:14.2: The ‘self’ or soul is here identified with the ‘world’ (i.e. any state of existence): the ‘self’ is held to be any one of the five aggregates, and the ‘world’ the other four (Comy).
mn102:15.2: For faith and the rest, see Sutta 95, para. 14.
